component.name: Bose Connect for Linux
component.summary: Drive a Bose QuietComfort or SoundLink over RFCOMM
Controla unos audífonos Bose QuietComfort o SoundLink sobre RFCOMM

description.p: Controls Bose Bluetooth headphones and speakers from Linux by speaking the same RFCOMM protocol as the official Bose Connect app. This package is the GTK4 + libadwaita front-end built on the bose_connect library. The project started as a fork of the C program Denton-L/based-connect and was rewritten in Rust.

It shows the battery with its recent history, playback controls, the settings each device supports (noise cancelling or audio modes, self-voice, voice prompts and language, auto-off, pairing mode), the paired sources, and whether this computer has a working audio stream to the device. It keeps one connection open per session, sends low-battery notifications and has a tray icon; the last device is remembered in ~/.config/bose-connect/state.json.

Party and stereo mode for two SoundLink Color II speakers: join them with this computer or a phone as the music source, switch between party and stereo, and separate them. From this computer the app joins once the audio has been quiet for a minute, restarts the audio stream after a mode change, and can make PipeWire use 44.1 kHz. A late reply from a device no longer drops the connection.

The library and the command line add party and stereo mode for two SoundLink Color II speakers and support for the NC 700 Headphones (stepped noise cancelling, favourites, motion auto-off and more). Fixes reading the paired-device list when no device has an audio link and the QC35 II's pairing-mode reply.

The GUI now controls a real device over one persistent connection, redraws only when the device state changes, and shows whether this computer has a working audio stream to the device, with a hint to reconnect when it does not. Adds QuietComfort 45 support (audio modes, equalizer, shortcut, self-voice), pairing mode on the SoundLink Color II, and a grouped command-line help.

The GUI is still a mockup on a simulated device. The protocol library reads every reply from its header, fixes the paired-device commands, adds RFCOMM channel 1 as a fallback and adds the QC Ultra Headphones settings (equalizer, immersive audio, auto-off and more).

Redesigned single-page control panel (still a mockup: it runs on a simulated device and is not yet connected to the library), with volume and media-transport controls. The protocol library adds volume, media keys, active-source and own-address commands, and QC Ultra Headphones support.

First GUI release. Hero battery card, four setting tiles, four profiles, paired-devices panel, and a live activity log. KDE Plasma 6 libnotify integration verified end-to-end. Tray icon and BlueZ discovery are scaffolded; full D-Bus bindings land in a follow-up.
